target_customer: Software companies, from startups to Fortune 500, that need to send webhooks to their own customers
problem: Sending webhooks reliably needs retries, deliverability, security and monitoring that differ from the rest of the stack, and teams keep rebuilding it.
business_model: Usage and tier based SaaS and open-source core with a hosted cloud

founders.name: Tom Hacohen
previous_startups: An unnamed earlier company whose customers kept asking for webhooks (Twilio founder spotlight)
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he has been coding since age 9. Employers and education not found in opened sources.

competitors.name: HostedHooks
competitors.what: Hosted service for sending webhooks to customers

competitors.name: Webhooks.io
competitors.what: Webhook delivery service named by VentureBeat as a competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable multi-tenant delivery with retries, signing and observability at scale is standard distributed systems work with some hard parts; the company says it later delivered billions of webhooks.

defensibility.rationale: Open source core lowers lock-in fear but customer integrations and the Standard Webhooks spec it authored create some switching cost; teams could still build their own.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Svix; VentureBeat said Svix viewed Zapier as complementary.

market_need_then: Founder said customers of his previous company repeatedly asked for webhooks and a friend asked about them in a Slack community, showing recurring demand; Aleph described webhooks as the nervous system of SaaS.

branding.name_origin: The company blog says the name was chosen because its sound and look express speed, robustness and simplicity; where the word itself came from is not stated.
branding.domain_note: Operates on svix.com; history not found.

identity.logo: An S made of two pieces with the gap forming a river suggesting information flow (company blog)
identity.visual_style: Clean developer-tool look; uppercase and lowercase forms look nearly identical
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical, for example Ship webhooks in days, not quarters

branding.brand_signature: Creator of the Standard Webhooks specification

rebrands.why: Team decided the original name did not reflect its values; date not stated in the opened snippet

branding.community_and_virality: Authored the Standard Webhooks specification, an open standard, per the company site.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among developers through open source and the Standard Webhooks spec, with a logo and rebrand rationale, but no evidence of mass community or merch.

outcome_analysis: Svix started as Diahook, took a 2.6 million dollar pre-seed in November 2021 from YC and Aleph, and raised a round led by a16z in February 2023. It lists customers such as Brex, Twilio, PagerDuty and Vanta, claims billions of webhooks delivered, and published the Standard Webhooks spec. It is still Active with a small team and no exit. Its success rests on a clear developer pain, an open source go-to-market and low competition at the start.
notes: The February 2023 round is called Series A with 10.4M by an aggregator and 7.75M by another; the company post and a16z give no amount or stage so it is recorded as other with no amount. Total raised of about 13M is aggregator only and not recorded. Rebrand date from Diahook not opened. Launch HN of June 2021 exists per a blog mirror. Competitor sources are dated November 2021, after the batch. Hookdeck existed around then but no dated source was opened so it is not listed.
